items.title: Major players Lenskart, Groww, Adani Energy join MSCI India Index
items.description: MSCI announced changes to India indices, adding four stocks and removing three.  India's weight in the MSCI India Standard Index will rise slightly to 11.9 percent.  Lenskart Solutions and Adani Energy Solutions are among the new inclusions.  Astral and Balkrishna Industries will move to the Smallcap Index after exclusion.  These changes will take effect on August 31, impacting fund flows.

items.title: Top FPIs ride out storm, outrun Nifty & Sensex in Q1
items.description: During the June quarter, leading international funds encountered remarkable gains within Indian equities, significantly boosting their reported portfolio values. This strong performance exceeded that of key Indian stock market indices, primarily driven by astute investments in mid- and small-cap companies, reinforcing India's reputation as a promising landscape for discerning stock pickers.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: Indian equity markets experienced a slight decline on Thursday, influenced by elevated crude oil prices. Investors remained cautious due to positioning ahead of the weekly Sensex expiry, despite a supportive global outlook. The Nifty50 and Sensex both closed marginally lower, reflecting a market lacking strong directional triggers. Elevated crude prices and geopolitical uncertainty kept domestic investors hesitant, suggesting a range-bound market.

items.title: For Friday | Stocks in news: Indigo Paints, LG Electronics India, Tata Motors PV, Honasa Consumer, Ashok Leyland and Physicswallah in focus
items.description: Indian equity markets saw a decline on Thursday, August 13, with the Nifty 50 closing lower. Persistent Middle East tensions and a stronger US dollar influenced investor sentiment negatively. Several companies like Indigo Paints and LG Electronics India reported their first-quarter earnings results. Other firms such as Ashok Leyland and Physicswallah will release their results on Friday. Corporate developments and earnings will guide trading in upcoming sessions.

items.title: Bank of America's $1.9 billion Jio bet shows global banks want a slice of India's retail lending market
items.description: Bank of America is set to invest a substantial $1.9 billion into Jio Financial's Jio Credit, marking a significant show of confidence in India's booming retail loan sector. This collaboration merges Jio's innovative digital capabilities with the seasoned financial knowledge of Bank of America, enabling a strategic expansion in the rapidly growing Indian economy. Regulatory approvals will be required to finalize this impactful venture.

items.title: Corporate cover rates decline amid ample capacity
items.description: Insurance rates for fire, cyber, professional indemnity and directors’ liability fell sharply in the June quarter as abundant capacity intensified competition. Marsh India expects the buyer-friendly market to persist, with companies using lower prices to secure broader coverage and higher limits.

items.title: Karnataka HC quashes ED money laundering case against Sammaan Capital
items.description: The Karnataka High Court has quashed ED money-laundering proceedings against Sammaan Capital, formerly Indiabulls Housing Finance, ruling that the case could not continue after its underlying predicate offences ceased to sustain the allegations.

items.title: LEAP India shares to list today. Check GMP ahead of debut
items.description: LEAP India IPO:  The public issue, which was open for subscription between August 7 and August 11, was subscribed 8.38 times overall. The retail investor portion was booked 1.71 times, while the qualified institutional buyers (QIB) category saw 16.84 times subscription and the non-institutional investor (NII) segment was subscribed 12.64 times.

items.title: Technocraft Ventures shares to list today. GMP signals 17% listing gains ahead of debut
items.description: The healthy GMP comes after an impressive subscription response. The IPO, which was open from August 7 to August 11, was subscribed 38.69 times overall, reflecting robust investor appetite across investor categories.

items.title: These large- and mid-cap stocks can give more than 25% return in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: Looking at what happens in the short term is important, as it does have an impact on stock prices. But also always keep an eye on the macro picture. Consider, for instance, this important change: FIIs are no longer the only large source of equity flows. DII money has become much more significant over the years. That does not make the market immune to foreign selling; but it does mean that sustained selling by FIIs need not produce the kind of market reaction it once did.
